explanation: Scan from west to east, which is reverse input order. A building is visible exactly when it is strictly taller than all buildings already scanned; strict comparison handles equal-height blocking.
timeComplexity: O(n) time. Reverse scans visit each building once; stack scans push/pop each building at most once.
spaceComplexity: O(v) output space for v visible buildings; O(1) other space. Reverse scans retain a running maximum; forward scans additionally retain candidate buildings.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: When scanning west to east, maximum is the tallest building strictly west of the current one. The current building sees the sunset exactly when it exceeds that maximum. A nonvisible building cannot change the maximum; a visible one becomes the new maximum. Appending visible indices during this reverse scan already produces the required west-to-east order.
walkthrough: For east-to-west heights [5, 9, 4, 7, 3], begin at westernmost index 4: height 3 is visible. Index 3, height 7, is taller and visible. Height 4 at index 2 is blocked. Height 9 at index 1 is visible; height 5 at index 0 is blocked. Return indices [4, 3, 1].
edgeCases: Equal-height western buildings block earlier buildings because the comparison is strict.
The westernmost building is visible, even if its height equals int.MinValue.
